first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both currently declining, and prior evidence indicates that shortening onboarding improved completion and time-to-value across self-serve accounts. I will verify the strongest directly relevant archived record before acting. A small guarded test can address the immediate funnel decline while protecting qualified activation and downstream revenue; success should require improvement in meaningful activation and qualified revenue, not completion alone. Promotional pricing may help price-sensitive SMB acquisition, but it risks margin and revenue quality and is less directly tied to the current activation and onboarding deterioration.

final.rationale: Run a standard A/B test of a shorter onboarding flow this week. The verified source found completion up 13%, time-to-value reduced by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention up 3%, making it directly relevant to the current 4% onboarding and 6% activation declines. Evaluate not only completion but meaningful activation, qualified revenue, and retention to avoid optimizing for shallow starts. Existing signup-simplification and in-product activation-messaging evidence supports the mechanism, while the test preserves uncertainty about current-segment effects and downstream revenue quality.
